lessons.title: Selectors & Specificity

sections.content: CSS selectors define which HTML elements on a page receive specific styles. Mastering selectors is fundamental — they give you granular control to style elements individually, in groups, or based on element relationships.

sections.title: Did you know?
sections.content: Specificity determines which CSS rule wins when multiple rules target the same element. An ID selector (#id) is more specific than a class selector (.class), which is more specific than an element selector (p).
Element selectors target all tags of a type. Class selectors (.) target elements sharing a class name. ID selectors (#) target a single unique element.

You can combine selectors to target nested elements. Descendant selectors (space), child selectors (>), and grouped selectors (comma) allow precise matching. Specificity is calculated based on weights: Inline (1000) > ID (100) > Class (10) > Element (1).

objectives: Understand element, class, ID, and universal selectors
Use selector combinators to target nested HTML elements
Calculate CSS specificity weights to resolve styling conflicts
lessons.mentorTip: Favor class selectors for reusable styling. Relying heavily on ID selectors can lead to specificity battles that make CSS difficult to debug.

lessons.title: The Box Model

sections.content: Every element in CSS is a rectangular box. The CSS Box Model governs how the dimensions of these boxes are computed — comprising Content, Padding, Border, and Margin layers.

sections.title: Essential Tip
sections.content: Setting 'box-sizing: border-box' forces padding and border to be included within the element's total width and height, preventing unexpected overflow layout bugs!
The Four Layers of the Box Model

1. Content: The area where text and images appear.
2. Padding: Transparent space surrounding content inside the border.
3. Border: The line surrounding the padding and content.
4. Margin: Transparent space outside the border separating elements.

objectives: Identify content, padding, border, and margin components of the Box Model
Understand default content-box vs border-box sizing behaviors
Control element spacing, width, height, and alignment effectively
lessons.mentorTip: Use dev tools (Inspect Element) to view the visual Box Model breakdown diagram for any element on a webpage.
